entries.test: Reproducible evaluations of LLM reliability on deterministic workplace tasks, including tasks selected from natural-language instructions, would test the claim.
entries.note: The normalization omits the particular emphasis on selecting actions through interpretation of human language.

entries.test: Comparisons of advertised agent capabilities with reproducible performance across marketed products would establish whether most fail to deliver those capabilities.
entries.note: “As sold” anchors the claim to advertised functionality.

entries.test: OpenClaw deployment documentation, operating costs, and reproducible tests of its advertised tasks would test the claimed requirements and poor performance.
entries.note: The normalization drops the comparative cost claim and the asserted deployment requirements.

entries.note: The surrounding discussion supports the reference to agent products.

entries.note: The normalization omits his uncertainty about economic effects as distinct from productivity.

entries.test: Public training expenditure histories and documentation of model maintenance and post-training would establish whether training is a recurring and growing operating requirement.
